about.content:
I began my programming journey in high school about eight years ago, focusing on UI design and frontend development. Over the past two years of my professional career, I have expanded my skills in backend development and database management, becoming more adaptable and eager to learn.
Through both university studies and professional work, I have gained strong teamwork experience, actively engaging in code reviews, project planning, and team discussions. My four years as a tutor have also strengthened my communication and teaching skills.
I am a fast learner who enjoys collaboration and continuous self-improvement, aiming to create projects that combine functionality with excellent user experience.

items.title: QA Intern – Codibly S.A.
items.description: My first job in the IT sector, completed as part of a high school internship program. It was a period of intensive learning, during which I gained insight into teamwork dynamics and the software development and testing process. I participated in training sessions, project meetings, and daily tasks, gradually improving my technical skills and understanding of industry best practices.
responsibilities: Conducting stress tests using JMeter
Writing tests for frontend components
Performing manual unit tests and reporting results
Participating in training sessions on software testing methodologies
Attending team meetings focused on work organization and task planning
Developing simple web applications to enhance technical skills

items.title: Technical Assistant – Aptiv Services Poland
items.description: My second internship, completed as part of my high school program, focused more strongly on working with network systems and their physical maintenance. I was responsible for assembling integrated circuits, providing technical support to senior staff, and developing simple Python scripts for testing closed network systems.
responsibilities: Maintaining physical network and electronic infrastructure
Installing and testing integrated circuits and hardware components
Providing helpdesk and on-site technical support
Developing simple Python scripts for testing and diagnostics
Troubleshooting and performing minor hardware repairs

items.title: Tutor – Edualy
items.description: During my work as a tutor, I developed strong communication skills, patience, and an individualized approach to students. I learned how to explain complex concepts in an accessible way, foster motivation, and support the development of analytical thinking and independent problem-solving skills.
responsibilities: Preparing students for final exams in computer science, mathematics, and physics
Conducting lessons for vocational exam preparation
Providing academic-level tutoring in web technologies, algorithms, and data structures

items.title: Junior Software Developer – Codibly
items.description: As a member of the development team, I participated in the implementation of commercial projects in the fields of e-mobility and renewable energy. My work involved designing and developing solutions for both client-side and server-side applications, as well as actively contributing to planning, requirements analysis, and process optimization within the team. I collaborated directly with clients, presented project progress, proposed functional improvements, and provided UX/UI design advice. Additionally, I supported the intern recruitment process and continuously expanded my technical skills by learning new technologies.
responsibilities: Designing and implementing frontend and backend functionalities
Collaborating with the project team on requirement refinement and sprint planning
Maintaining and extending existing system modules
Participating in daily Scrum meetings and code reviews
Assisting in intern recruitment and supporting their technical growth
Regularly presenting project progress and deliverables to the client
Learning and adopting new technologies in response to project needs
Providing active input on design and UX/UI aspects

items.title: Node.js Developer – Solidstudio
items.description: As a member of the technical support team, I work on maintaining and improving the company’s core product, which delivers e-mobility solutions to clients worldwide. I am responsible for direct communication with clients, verifying and resolving reported issues, and implementing new functionalities based on their requirements. Additionally, I contribute to the development of an AI-based tool aimed at automating the most time-consuming aspects of ticket evaluation and handling.
responsibilities: Fixing bugs and implementing features based on client requests
Communicating directly with clients and participating in requirement planning and analysis
Acting as a technical expert in the field of e-mobility protocols
Regularly monitoring infrastructure status and responding to recurring issues
Developing an AI-based tool aimed at optimizing client support ticket handling

githubCard.title: View More on GitHub
githubCard.subtitle: Explore all my repositories and side projects.

items.name: Weather App
items.description:
The Weather App is a full-stack application that provides weather forecasts, along with estimates of energy generated by photovoltaic panels for the upcoming week, based on the user's geolocation.
The frontend is built with React and Material UI, and it uses my Node.js endpoint. The application also offers a dark mode feature.

items.name: IOTA Network Visualizer
items.description:
A lightweight IOTA network dashboard for visualizing live blockchain activity, validator data, epochs, and checkpoints.
The app is built with React, TypeScript, and Vite, using IOTA JSON-RPC endpoints to fetch network data. It includes interactive charts powered by Chart.js and a 3D validator globe built with Three.js and Globe.gl.

items.name: Color Lines
items.description:
This project is a replica of the widely available Color Lines game, also known as Match 5.
From a technical standpoint, it involves a grid of div elements generated at random positions with randomly colored balls.
The core of the game is the Depth-First Search (DFS) algorithm for pathfinding. Written almost entirely in TypeScript.

items.name: Bot Shooter
items.description:
An <orange>AI-driven</orange> arena shooter built with <orange>Pygame</orange>, where bots navigate, detect enemies, and engage in combat. The goal is to reach 5 kills as quickly as possible.

Bots compete in a closed arena, collecting resources and eliminating opponents. Their behavior is driven by a <orange>state machine</orange>, and the map is represented as a graph with an <orange>A* pathfinding</orange>.

items.name: Hunters and Beasts
items.description:
A web application supporting a multiplayer board game about hunters tracking dangerous beasts.

The project combines a Vue frontend with a FastAPI backend, handling real-time game state through WebSockets. Core mechanics include state-driven AI behaviors for beasts, turn management, and interactive map-based gameplay.

items.name: Physics Simulation
items.description: This project is a collection of interactive <orange>physics simulations</orange> created using <orange>Pygame</orange>. It includes implementations of systems such as <orange>mass-spring models</orange>, <orange>cloth simulation</orange> with <orange>Verlet integration</orange>, and <orange>collision mechanics</orange> for soft and rigid bodies, accompanied by visual representations and detailed mathematical formulas included in the README.

items.name: MP3 Player
items.description:
A project that serves as a music player with an interface and the ability to upload custom playlists.
Most of the project focuses on the Node.js backend, which handles reading music albums from the internal project folder and storing user-uploaded albums.

items.name: Snake Game
items.description:
Snake Game was essentially my first encounter with programming, created during Client-Side Application classes in my first year of high school.
The project is based on a simple interval, randomly generates the fruit position, and uses a straightforward collision mechanism. I must admit that its presence here is primarily due to nostalgia.
